title: Post-session knowledge check
notes: PROVISIONAL INSTRUMENT. These items were drafted for the FarmSim prototype and have NOT been reviewed or approved by a supervisor. Review and revise before any study use. Editing this file is enough to change the instrument - no code changes are required. The post-test uses the same eight items as the pre-test, presented in a different order, so that the two scores are directly comparable.

questions.text: At which stage is maize most sensitive to a shortage of water?
options: Immediately after planting
Around flowering, when the tassels and silks appear
Once the cobs have already dried
Maize is equally sensitive at every stage
questions.explanation: Water shortage around flowering has a much larger effect on the final yield than a shortage at most other stages.

questions.text: Why does a delay in responding to a pest outbreak matter?
options: It does not matter as long as you treat before harvest
Pest numbers and the damage they cause keep increasing, and the problem can spread to neighbouring plants
Pests only damage plants on the day they arrive
Delaying makes treatment more effective
questions.explanation: Untreated pests keep feeding and can move to nearby plants, so the same outbreak costs more the longer it is left.

questions.text: Irrigating in the middle of a hot, windy day usually wastes water. Why?
options: Water applied at midday is more likely to be lost to evaporation before the plants can use it
Plants stop taking up water while the sun is out
Midday water damages maize leaves
Soil cannot absorb water while it is warm
questions.explanation: Evaporation losses are highest when it is hot and windy, so the same amount of water goes further early in the morning or late in the afternoon.

questions.text: What happens when far more water is applied to a tile than the soil can hold?
options: The extra water drains past the roots and is wasted
The crop grows proportionally faster
The extra water is stored for later in the season
The crop becomes immune to drought
questions.explanation: Soil can only hold so much water. Anything beyond that drains below the root zone and is lost, which is expensive when the reserve is shared and limited.

questions.text: A block of maize was left dry for a long stretch of the season and lost condition. It is then watered well for the rest of the season. What should you expect?
options: It fully catches up with the rest of the field
It produces more than the rest of the field because of the extra water
It recovers partly, but the yield from that block stays lower
It makes no difference either way
questions.explanation: Damage done during a stress period is not fully undone by watering afterwards, which is why keeping a crop out of stress matters more than rescuing it later.

questions.text: The water reserve is nearly empty and there is still a lot of field left. What is generally the better decision?
options: Spread the remaining water thinly across every plant
Concentrate the remaining water on part of the field so those plants stay out of stress
Stop watering entirely and hope for rain
Water only the plants that already look worst
questions.explanation: Giving every plant less than it needs can leave the whole field stressed. Keeping a smaller area properly watered usually protects more of the harvest.

questions.text: Why is the soil prepared before the seed goes in?
options: To make the field look tidy
To loosen the seedbed so seed sits in good contact with soil and roots and water can move into it
To dry the soil out before planting
It is only done because of tradition
questions.explanation: A loosened seedbed gives better seed-to-soil contact and lets roots and water move through the soil more easily.

questions.text: What is the most reliable way to pick up a pest problem early?
options: Wait until damage is visible from the edge of the field
Walk through the field regularly and inspect plants closely, including under the leaves
Treat the whole field on a fixed schedule whether or not pests are present
Judge it from the colour of the soil
questions.explanation: Regular scouting finds a problem while it is still small and still confined to a few plants.
